newsitem.title: USA: Union Camp to cut 400 jobs, take $47 million charge.
newsitem.headline: Union Camp to cut 400 jobs, take $47 million charge.

text.p: Union Camp Corp., reacting to tightening conditions in the paper industry, said on Monday it will cut about 400 jobs and take a one-time, pre-tax charge of $47 million for restructuring and asset write-downs.
The company said the charge, to be taken in the current quarter, will reduce its 1996 after-tax profits by about $29 million, or 42 cents a share.
Union Camp, based in Wayne, N.J., said the moves were designed to add as much as $100 million to the company's pre-tax earning power over the next 18 to 24 months.
The company, which had 1995 sales of $4.2 billion, is a leading manufacturer and marketer of paper, packaging, chemicals and wood products.
"The paper industry is changing, and Union Camp is moving aggressively to capitalise on these changes," Chairman W. Craig McClelland said in a statement.

"The capital-intensive nature of this industry, which is operating in a global marketplace of low to moderate economic growth and inflation, requires that we be even more disciplined in the future regarding cost control, asset returns and targeted growth," he said.
The company said it expects about two-thirds of the $100 million of added earning power to come from cost reductions and asset realignments.
The company, which has more than 18,000 employees, said it would offer enhanced severance packages to about 400 workers as it reduces its work force over the next nine months.
"We are near completion of an in-depth review of all work areas in our corporation and, consequently, we see the opportunity to take significant costs out of our company," McClelland said.
The company said it plans to improve profitability with changes in its product and business mixes and aggressive investments in marketing. It also said it would realign portions of its assets.
"This process also involves write-downs of assets and the removal of equipment no longer required to meet the needs of our customers," McClelland said.
Union Camp's stock gained 37.5 cents to $48.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
